items.title: Mahalia Jackson Interview, 1955-07-26
items.q: I knew all about, um, Louis Armstrong and Papa Celestan. I've seen them all my life. And, uh, uh, Kid Kelly and Buck Johnson and all of them. I, uh, I knew all of those people. And, um, I met them.

ctx.x: Well, then you have done some church singing indeed. Now tell me, when you grew up, did you only hear the singing in the church? Or did you also hear the blues singing? Did you hear the jazz?

Oh, yes. I couldn't help from hearing it. I knew all about, um, Louis Armstrong and Papa Celestan. I've seen them all my life. And, uh, uh, Kid Kelly and Buck Johnson and all of them. I, uh, I knew all of those people. And, um, I met them. And they used to go to church too. That's why they can play these religious songs. Like, uh, uh, when the saints and, uh, what this other song, uh, we shall walk the streets of glory. And, uh, just a closer walk with these by and by when the morning comes. Because they were…

Well, I can see that on you when you are singing. You have a kind of, you close your eyes and you sort of listen into yourself. And you can, uh, the one who sees it can well understand that you are listening to what you are going to sing. Now, it must be rather difficult though, to, uh, make music, and also to arrange music, as I see you do, when you don't, can't write. How can you go about it?
